whys.why: Why does stripe-webhook.ts cast the parsed event to Stripe.Event?
whys.because: The Stripe SDK hands the webhook handler an untyped payload and its constructEvent returns the event typed only through its own declaration.

whys.why: Why does the Stripe SDK hand the handler an untyped payload?
whys.because: Webhook bodies arrive as raw bytes over HTTP, and the signature check must run over those exact bytes before any parsing.

whys.why: Why must the signature check run over the raw bytes?
whys.because: Stripe signs the bytes it sent, so any reformatting by a parser would change them and break verification.

whys.why: Why does Stripe sign the bytes it sent rather than a parsed form?
whys.because: An HMAC over the transmitted body is the only form both ends can reproduce without agreeing a canonical serialisation.
whys.evidence: RFC 2104 defines HMAC over an octet string.

whys.why: Why can both ends reproduce only an HMAC over the transmitted body?
whys.because: JSON has no canonical serialisation, so key order and whitespace differ between producers, and only the octets on the wire are shared.
whys.evidence: RFC 8259 leaves member order and whitespace to the producer.

whyChain.rootCause: JSON has no canonical serialisation, so the octets on the wire are the only shared form a signature can cover.
whyChain.rootCheck: On 2026-11-20, RFC 8259 still leaves member order and whitespace to the producer.
whyChain.readback: JSON has no canonical serialisation, therefore Stripe signs the raw octets, therefore the SDK hands an untyped payload, therefore stripe-webhook.ts casts the parsed event to Stripe.Event.
